title: Asking the living to pray with us does not extend to the dead, with whom we cannot communicate
source_text: XXXIII. Ad eum autem honorem, quem deferimus iis quibuscum hic versamur, aut quibuscum nobis est mutuum aliquod commercium, illud quoque pertinet, quod eos de quorum sumus pietate persuasi, rogare solemus, ut nos apud Deum precibus suis juvent, ac nobiscum postulent ea quibus egemus bona & auxilia. Nec enim quisquam virum pium procul degentem, & cum quo nullum potest epistolarum commercium habere, voce, vel corde rogabit, ut pro ipso Deum oret: ut si quis olim Hierosolymis Paulum Romae vinctum allocutus fuisset, & verbis, vel tacita & interiori loquela, precum ejus apud Deum auxilium implorasset. Inde est quod Protestantes & Reformati omnes, Sanctos in Christo defunctos, non perinde ac vivos, rogant ut illos suis orationibus apud Deum adjuvent. Quoniam, scilicet, illi procul a nobis beatitudine & gloria caelesti fruuntur: nec ulla ratio superest, qua possimus cum illis animi nostri sensa communicare.
pass_a_gloss: To that honor which we pay to those with whom we live here, or with whom we have some mutual commerce, this also belongs: that we are accustomed to ask those of whose piety we are persuaded to help us before God with their prayers, and to ask with us the goods and aids we need. For no one will ask, by voice or by heart, a pious man living far off, with whom he can have no commerce of letters, to pray to God for him: as if someone once at Jerusalem had addressed Paul bound at Rome, and by words, or by a silent and inward speech, had implored the help of his prayers before God. Hence it is that all Protestants and Reformed do not, as they do the living, ask the Saints who have died in Christ to help them before God with their prayers. Because they enjoy heavenly blessedness and glory far from us, and no way remains by which we can communicate the feelings of our mind to them.
pass_b_english: Asking trusted pious people to pray with us and for us belongs to honor among those with whom we have real dealings.
No one addresses, aloud or in the heart, a pious man too far away for even a letter, as if someone in Jerusalem had silently begged the help of Paul's prayers while Paul was in prison at Rome.
For that reason Protestants do not ask the dead in Christ, as they ask the living, to help them before God.
The blessed are far off in glory, and there is no way left to tell them what we feel.

choices.english: not in the same way as the living
choices.why: The refusal is of invocation of the dead, not of asking the living to pray.
rejected: they ask no one to pray
they pray to the dead in a relative sense
